case_title: NATIONAL BANK OF OMAN v. BARAKARA ABDUL AZIZ & ANR.
trial_court_outcome: Process issued for offences u/ss. 418 and 420
high_court_outcome: Quashed the complaint and directed the CJM to pass fresh orders following the procedure u/s. 202
neutral_facts: The accused opened a current account with the complainant bank, representing that he held an Indian passport. He gained the bank's confidence by providing a trading license and claiming to own a business in Abu Dhabi. Based on these representations, the bank granted an overdraft facility, which was later increased. The accused defaulted on repayments and entered into a restructuring agreement with the bank, issuing post-dated cheques for repayment. The cheques were dishonoured, and the accused absconded to India without discharging his loan liability. The complainant bank, which had no presence in India, appointed a power of attorney holder to file a complaint. The Chief Judicial Magistrate issued process for offences under sections 418 and 420 of the IPC, but the High Court quashed the order, stating that the CJM failed to follow the procedure under section 202 of the Cr.P.C. The matter was remitted to the Magistrate for passing fresh orders.
